summary: This note is a wiki-style overview of leptin, a hormone made mainly by fat cells that acts centrally on the hypothalamus to regulate hunger, energy use and fat mass, with secondary roles in reproduction, bone, immunity and inflammation. It covers its signalling via leptin receptors, its roles in the nervous, circulatory, reproductive and immune systems, genetic mutations, and its links to obesity, osteoarthritis, and therapy with the analog metreleptin. The text is cut off partway through the History section.
one_line: An overview of leptin, the fat-cell hormone that regulates appetite, energy balance, reproduction, bone and immunity, and its role in obesity and therapy.
key_facts: Leptin is produced predominantly by adipose cells and is described as the 'energy expenditure hormone'.
The primary function of leptin is the regulation of adipose tissue mass through central hypothalamus-mediated effects on hunger, food energy use, physical exercise and energy balance.
Leptin inhibits hunger in the lateral hypothalamus and stimulates satiety in the medial hypothalamus by promoting synthesis of α-MSH.
Ob-Rb is the only leptin receptor isoform that can signal intracellularly via the JAK-STAT and MAPK pathways, and it is present in hypothalamic nuclei.
The Ob(Lep) gene is located on chromosome 7 in humans, and human leptin is a 16-kDa protein of 167 amino acids.
Leptin was approved in the United States in 2014 for use in congenital leptin deficiency and generalized lipodystrophy.
Metreleptin (trade names Myalept, Myalepta) was first approved in Japan in 2013, in the United States in February 2014, and in Europe in 2018.
Leptin levels rise during pregnancy and fall after childbirth, and the placenta produces leptin.
Leptin along with kisspeptin controls the onset of puberty, and high leptin levels in obese females can trigger early menarche.
Leptin's role in regulating bone mass was identified in 2000, and leptin decreases cancellous bone while increasing cortical bone.
Obese individuals generally have higher circulating leptin than normal weight individuals, and this is attributed to leptin resistance.
A 2015 report described a two-year-old boy with extreme obesity and a homozygous transversion (c.298G → T) changing aspartic acid to tyrosine at position 100 (p.D100Y).
Leptin levels vary exponentially, not linearly, with fat mass, and are higher between midnight and early morning.
Leptin is being evaluated as a potential target for the treatment of anorexia nervosa, with short-term metreleptin treatment producing rapid beneficial cognitive, emotional and behavioral effects.
The NHS in England will commission metreleptin treatment for all with congenital leptin deficiency regardless of age beginning on April 1, 2019.

entities.name: Leptin
entities.role: Hormone made mainly by adipose cells that acts on the hypothalamus to regulate hunger, energy balance and fat mass

entities.name: Metreleptin
entities.role: Analog of human leptin used to treat complications of leptin deficiency and generalized lipodystrophy

entities.name: Leptin receptor
entities.role: Single-transmembrane type I cytokine receptor encoded by the LEPR gene, with six isoforms, of which Ob-Rb signals intracellularly

entities.name: LEPR
entities.role: Single gene encoding the six leptin receptor isoforms

entities.name: Ob(Lep) gene
entities.role: Gene for leptin, located on chromosome 7 in humans

entities.name: Neuropeptide Y
entities.role: Potent hunger promoter that leptin counteracts in the lateral hypothalamus

entities.name: α-MSH
entities.role: Hunger suppressant whose synthesis leptin promotes in the medial hypothalamus

entities.name: Anandamide
entities.role: Potent hunger promoter that binds the same receptors as THC and that leptin counteracts

entities.name: Amylin
entities.role: Hormone involved in gastric emptying and fullness that, with leptin, produced sustained weight loss in obese leptin-resistant rats

entities.name: Rosedale diet
entities.role: Fad diet based on ideas about leptin and weight, described as based on unsound science

entities.name: Human Genome Equivalent (HuGE) review
entities.role: 2004 review that found no association between leptin-related polymorphisms and obesity

entities.name: Taiwanese aborigines
entities.role: Population in a 2006 study linking the LEP-2548 G/A genotype to morbid obesity

entities.name: Japan
entities.role: Country where metreleptin was first approved in 2013

entities.name: United States
entities.role: Country where leptin was approved in 2014 and metreleptin approved in February 2014

entities.name: National Health Service in England
entities.role: Will commission metreleptin treatment for congenital leptin deficiency from April 1, 2019
